Supón que la clave es una ristra de bits: Suppose the key is a string of random bits, as long as the message, and that it is used only once. Eve intercepts the ciphertext $c$. What can she say about the message? Nothing, and it can be proved: for every possible message $m^{*}$ there is exactly one key, $k^{*} = c \oplus m^{*}$, that turns it into that very $c$. And since all the keys are equally likely, so are all the messages. The ciphertext in front of her is compatible with “attack at dawn”, with “retreat tonight” and with any other phrase of the same length.
